items.title: Court overturns adoption order involving foreign national
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court in Penang has allowed the National Registration Department (NRD) to challenge a court order directing it to issue a birth certificate to an adopted Chinese citizen. She ruled that the earlier court order, dated March 17, was null and void on the grounds of illegality or lack of jurisdiction as it required NRD to act contrary to the Adoption Act and the Births and Deaths Registration Act. However, on March 17, High Court judge Dr Choong Yeow Choy allowed their appeal and granted the adoption order.

items.title: 'Outside my knowledge': Jalaluddin responds to MB candidate issue
items.summary: JELEBU: Negri Sembilan Umno Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he was not informed of the sole menteri besar candidate submitted to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. He said the submission was made without his knowledge, stressing that it is the Umno president's prerogative to nominate a candidate for the post. Yesterday, Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said only one name had been submitted to Tuanku Muhriz for royal assent.

items.title: Chinese engineer pleads not guilty to endangering son at Nilai toll plaza
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A Chinese citizen who went viral for allegedly leaving his child near the Nilai toll plaza pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to exposing the 12-year-old to the risk of physical injury. According to the charge, Jiao, an engineer, had exposed the child in a manner likely to cause physical injury at 1.21pm at the Nilai toll plaza exit ramp. Counsel Shahmi Iffah Mohd Arshad requested minimum bail, arguing that Jiao is the family's sole breadwinner.

items.title: Anwar's defamation suit against Tuan Ibrahim to go to trial in May
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's defamation suit against Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man will go to trial next year. Anwar's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the five-day trial is scheduled for May 11 to 14 and May 28, with Dec 18 fixed for case management. Anwar filed the suit against Tuan Ibrahim in August.

items.title: Malaysia's Q3 economy expands faster than expected at 5.5pct
items.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia said the stronger growth was driven by sustained household spending, increased investment activities and improved export performance, particularly in technology-related products. The central bank said export growth strengthened further, driven by technology-related shipments of both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products. "Reflecting this strength, domestic E&E exports accelerated to 66.9 per cent year-on-year growth in the third quarter.

items.title: Malaysia's current account surplus hits RM5.7bil in Q3
items.summary: It said the goods account surplus expanded to RM56.2 billion from RM40.7 billion in the preceding quarter, as exports rose to RM409.7 billion from RM359.3 billion. Imports grew 17.9 per cent to RM97.3 billion, outpacing the 10.4 per cent increase in exports to RM90.4 billion. The primary income deficit also widened to RM41.8 billion from RM27.2 billion, driven by higher earnings of foreign companies operating in Malaysia, which reached RM64.3 billion during the quarter.

items.title: Myanmar mother among 9 migrants arrested in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A Myanmar mother who returned to Malaysia illegally in search of work to support her family was arrested with two friends after crossing the border from Thailand into Kelantan. After returning to Myanmar last month, she decided to come back to Malaysia to resume her job, bringing two friends, aged 18 and 28, with her. I need to find work in Malaysia to support my family.

items.title: Anwar calls for fairer trade, technology sharing at Apec CEO Summit
items.summary: SHENZHEN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told global and business leaders today there was a need for genuine multilateralism, equitable technology sharing and human-centric development. Speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Centre, the prime minister said global leaders and the business community must ensure economic progress does not marginalise emerging economies. "We must respect multilateral arrangements.

items.title: MP flags environmental, water concerns over Kapar industrial park
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An opposition member of parliament (MP) has asked whether the government had assessed the combined impact of a planned 1,623-acre industrial development in Bukit Kerayong, Kapar, on flooding, water supply, electricity and infrastructure. Halimah said Kapar already faced infrastructure problems, including overcrowded schools, recurring floods, damaged roads and pressure on its drainage system. Ugak said the Data Centre Task Force assessed every data centre application to ensure adequate electricity and water supplies before approval.

items.title: Anwar thanks Trump for recognising Malaysia's role in easing Cambodia-Thailand tensions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed appreciation for United States President Donald Trump's recognition of Malaysia's efforts in helping Thailand and Cambodia ease tensions and pursue peace. Anwar shared this in a Facebook post today regarding his participation in the Asean-United States Special Summit. Earlier, Trump acknowledged Anwar's role in helping broker a peace agreement between Cambodia and Thailand last year, while reaffirming Washington's commitment to its full implementation.

items.title: Xi and Putin to meet ahead of historic Trump trilateral summit
items.summary: SHENZHEN: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin were set to meet on Wednesday, a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in Shenzhen. Washington had signalled that Ukraine was not expected to be addressed — something Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem — before Trump said it would be. China has said only that the leaders would hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations" on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting.

items.title: China's Xi calls for greater international cooperation on AI
items.summary: SHENZHEN: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade, as pressure grows on world powers to do more to address the risks of the groundbreaking technology. Xi made the remarks as he formally opened an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet US President Donald Trump on Thursday. "Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.

items.title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations. Harvey Jones, the chair of the company's board, said in an earnings call that "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

items.title: Police van tragedy highlights need for stronger vehicle safety
items.summary: I AM deeply saddened by the tragic accident involving a police van near Tapah on the North-South Expressway, which claimed the life of 26-year-old Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Alif Yaacob and left 10 other police personnel injured. Police personnel travelling on official duties must be assured that the vehicles they use are safe, roadworthy and properly maintained. Second, the safety of police personnel travelling in official vehicles must be given priority.

items.title: Perlis detects illegal female-only e-hailing services
items.summary: PADANG BESAR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) in Perlis has detected illegal e-hailing services operated by female drivers exclusively for passengers of the same gender. During the same period, the department issued 31 notices for various offences related to illegal passenger transport services and seized 14 vehicles. Between January and October, the department issued 1,068 notices and seized 16 Thai-registered vehicles for various traffic offences.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 18, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Wednesday, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street as technology-led selling and concerns over disruptions affecting major US systems weighed on investor sentiment. Market sentiment was further dampened by reported outages affecting the National Security Agency network, Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration. The benchmark index opened 0.7 points lower at 1,574.45.

items.title: Heavy rain triggers floods in 23 areas across Selangor
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Heavy rainfall, with recorded levels ranging from 63.5mm to 114.5mm, triggered floods in 23 areas across four districts in Selangor yesterday. The affected districts were Klang, with 8 areas, followed by Gombak (7), Kuala Selangor (5) and Petaling (3). "In Klang, the affected areas included Kampung Delek and Kampung Rantau Panjang, which each recorded 95.5mm of rainfall, followed by Kampung Jalan Kebun at 94.5mm.

items.title: 99 Speed Mart shares rise on firmer Q3 earnings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd shares rose in early trading after a strong performance in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026). In a filing with Bursa Malaysia yesterday, the company said its net profit rose to RM189.78 million in Q3 2026 from RM163.24 million in the corresponding quarter last year. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) expects 99 Speed Mart's steady sales volume growth to be sustained, supported by its staples-oriented product mix and highly accessible outlet locations.

items.title: Bank of Japan governor says central bank should keep raising rates
items.summary: TOKYO: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Wednesday the central bank should continue raising interest rates while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2.0 per cent target. Speaking in parliament, Ueda said it was important to see underlying inflation anchored around 2.0 per cent over time and conduct monetary policy appropriately to ensure that this could be achieved. "Given that financial conditions are still accommodative, it would be appropriate to continue raising the policy rate and adjust the degree of monetary easing in line with developments in the economy, prices and financial conditions," Ueda said.

items.title: Rubber tapper couple's dream inspires 46 doctors across four generations
items.summary: The dream of the late Loo Siew Chin and her husband, Lim Tang Too, grew into a remarkable family legacy, with eight of their 11 children becoming doctors. Their eldest son, Datuk Dr Lim Boon Sho, 81, said 34 of them are specialists serving in Malaysia and abroad, including in the United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland and Scotland. [[nid:1580298]] Also sharing their experiences were six of Boon Sho's siblings: Dr Lim Boon Sin, 77; Dr Lim Boon Ben, 75; Dr Lim Boon Seng, 73; Dr Lim Boon Hock, 68; Dr Lim Boon Han, 64; and Karin Lim Ai Ching, 66, a lawyer.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz tells Ismail to continue as MB, resignation undecided [WATCH]
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The position of Datuk Ismail Lasim as Negri Sembilan menteri besar remains unresolved after he had an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap yesterday. State government agencies also continued to identify Ismail as Negri Sembilan menteri besar at official events he attended or officiated. Earlier, the Negri Sembilan Palace, in a statement issued by Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali, said a menteri besar's resignation would only take effect after receiving Tuanku Muhriz's consent, in accordance with the Negri Sembilan State Constitution.

items.title: Education Ministry receives 73,498 Year One applications from six-year-olds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry received 73,498 applications for Year One admission under the 2027 Academic Calendar from six-year-olds as at Sept 30. The figure forms part of the total 491,649 applications received for Year One admission next year, including 418,151 applications from seven-year-old children. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry had decided to expand access to Year One by allowing parents to enrol their six-year-old children from the 2027 Academic Calendar.

items.title: US export curbs threaten to delay Malaysia's data centre projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's construction sector could face delays in data centre-related contract awards following new United States export controls, although local contractors have limited direct exposure to projects involving entities from D5 countries. According to CIMB Securities, ground checks indicated that most listed Malaysian contractors had limited direct involvement in turnkey data centre construction projects involving D5-country entities, reducing the risk of outright project cancellations. "Nevertheless, we believe the new US export controls may rekindle concerns over the pace of future data centre-related contract awards for the sector," it said in a note.

items.title: High Court: Developers cannot escape liability for recurring defects
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Property developers cannot escape liability for construction defects even after the defect liability period (DLP) has expired, the High Court has ruled. She said developers remained responsible for poor workmanship despite having carried out repairs, particularly when defects persisted or recurred. The purchasers claimed that their properties had numerous defects, including cracks, water leaks, staining, uneven finishes and alleged structural deficiencies.

items.title: US AI chip curbs threaten YTL Power's data centre growth, CIMB warns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tighter United States (US) restrictions on access to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips could slow future data centre capacity expansion at YTL Power International Bhd, potentially weighing on its earnings forecasts, although its existing contracted capacity is expected to remain unaffected. The firm said its base case assumed YTL Power's existing 298 megawatts (MW) of contracted co-location data centre capacity in Kulai, Johor, would remain intact, given its understanding that the lease agreements with tenants were firm. CIMB Securities estimated that if future capacity additions were halved to 100 MW annually from its current assumption of 200 MW, YTL Power's total contracted capacity would reach 678 MW by end-2030, compared with its current forecast of 1,078 MW.

items.title: Malaysia's semiconductor sector to weather US-China tech tensions, says PublicInvest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's semiconductor sector is expected to remain resilient amid escalating United States (US)-China technology tensions, according to Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest). Analyst Chong Hoe Leong said companies with diversified customer exposure and capabilities in precision engineering, automated testing and inspection were better positioned to navigate the changing regulatory environment. The US administration has introduced additional restrictions to prevent Chinese companies from circumventing existing semiconductor export controls by accessing advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips through overseas data centres.

items.title: Hap Seng Plantations earnings set for Q4 lift despite softer palm oil prices
items.summary: RHB Research said Hap Seng Plantations's FFB output rose 11 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and five per cent year-on-year (YoY) in Q3 FY26, supported by seasonally higher production despite drier weather conditions during the quarter. "We therefore maintain our FY26 to FY28 FFB growth assumptions at 7.1 per cent, 4.8 per cent and 7.0 per cent, for now," it said. Hap Seng Plantations's core profit improved 18.9 per cent QoQ and 59.2 per cent YoY in Q3 FY26, bringing its nine-month core earnings to RM123.24 million, up 25.8 per cent YoY.

items.title: Macron's wife braves rain to climb Batu Caves [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron's wife Brigitte braved heavy rain to climb the 272 steps to Batu Caves, drawing attention after a video of their visit went viral. The brief footage, posted on TikTok by NayLinKhant yesterday, showed Brigitte climbing the staircase to Sri Subramaniar Temple, accompanied by a large entourage and tight security. As rain poured down, members of the escort team tried to shield Brigitte from getting wet.

items.title: 77 Melaka residents evacuated as floods hit three districts
items.summary: MELAKA: Continuous heavy rain since yesterday evening has forced 77 residents from 20 families across three districts to evacuate to two temporary relief centres. In a statement, the Melaka State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said Melaka Tengah recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 50 people from 13 families housed at the Japerun Pantai Kundor relief centre since 10.04pm last night. "Jasin recorded 17 victims from three families following flash floods since 3.30pm, though no relief centre was opened," it said.

items.title: Two killed, one injured in Gerik-Jeli highway crash
items.summary: GERIK: Two people were killed while another was injured after a car collided with a lorry at Km49 of the Gerik-Jeli East-West Highway early today. District police chief Superintendent Abdul Samad Othman said the accident occurred at 1.15am when a Honda Civic travelling from Jeli towards Gerik lost control while negotiating a left-hand bend. He said the car, driven by a 36-year-old woman, then entered the opposite lane and collided with the lorry travelling from Gerik towards Jeli.
